TASHA CERDA, Mayor  MINA SEMENZA, City Clerk

If you would like to participate in this meeting, you can participate via the following
options:
  1. VIEW THE MEETING live on SPECTRUM CHANNEL 22 or ONLINE at
  youtube.com/CityofGardena

  2. PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING by emailing the Deputy City Clerk at
  publiccomment@cityofgardena.org by 5:00p.m. on the day of the meeting and write
  "Public Comment" in the subject line.

  3. ATTEND THE MEETING IN PERSON

  PUBLIC COMMENT: The City Council will hear from the public on any item on the
  agenda or any item of interest that is not on the agenda at the following times:
  Agenda Items – At the time the City Council considers the item or during Oral
  Communications
  Non-agenda Items – During Oral Communications
  Public Hearings – At the time for Public Hearings listed on the Agenda
  If you wish to address the Council, please complete a “Speaker Request” form and
  present it to the City Clerk or Sergeant of Arms. You will be called to the podium by
  name when it is your turn to address the Council. The City Council cannot legally take
  action on any item not scheduled on the Agenda. Such items may be referred for
  administrative action or scheduled on a future Agenda. Members of the public wishing to
  address the City Council will be given three (3) minutes to speak.

  4. The City of Gardena, in complying with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA),
  requests individuals who require special accommodations to access, attend and/or
  participate in the City meeting due to disability, to please contact the City Clerk's Office
  by phone (310) 217-9565 or email cityclerk@cityofgardena.org at least 24 business
  hours prior to the scheduled general meeting to ensure assistance is provided. Assistive
  listening devices are available.

  1
 STANDARDS OF BEHAVIOR THAT PROMOTE CIVILITY AT ALL PUBLIC MEETINGS

  Treat everyone courteously;
  Listen to others respectfully;
  Exercise self-control;
  Give open-minded consideration to all viewpoints;
  Focus on the issues and avoid personalizing debate; and
  Embrace respectful disagreement and dissent as democratic rights, inherent
  components of an inclusive public process, and tools for forging sound decisions

Thank you for your attendance and cooperation

  20. COUNCIL DIRECTIVES

  1) Council Member Love

  Subject - Staff is directed to include in the future discussions about the number of years
  between the selection honoree, a provision is discussed to disqualify city staff from being
  appointed to the Ad Hoc Committee for the “Wall of Fame.” This ensures that only
  community members serve on the selection committee.

  Purpose – The purpose of this directive is to eliminate any potential conflicts of interest.
  It prevents city staff from having influence over the selection of honorees. This ensures
  a fair and impartial process that upholds the integrity of the recognition.
  Reason – To maintain transparency and community ownership of the nomination
  process.

  Benefit – This directive reinforces public trust by ensuring the “Wall of Fame” remains a
  community-driven honor. Residents will feel confident that selections are made based
  solely on merit and public input. It protects the city’s reputation by maintaining fairness,
  neutrality, and transparency in the process.

  Council Member Francis seconded it.

  Purpose – To keep Council informed on progress of various projects
  Reason – To improve the aesthetic quality and beautification of our city.
  Benefit – To improve the quality of life in our city.

  22. COUNCIL REMARKS

  1) COUNCIL MEMBER FRANCIS – She thanked the staff for all their hard work, due
  diligence, and for answering her questions. She mentioned a lot is going on in our world
  and our city; it's important to recognize that many of these occurrences are wrong. She
  mentioned she is asking everyone to pay attention to what's going on because your
  children and your grandchildren are going to know what is going on; you keep hearing
  the words "unprecedented" and "historical." She continued to say it’s important that we
  pay close attention and to be sure that elections have consequences and we have to
  make sure that people and our children understand; these are challenging times, and
  difficult times but better days are coming; it's been promised.

  2) COUNCIL MEMBER HENDERSON - Since the last meeting, he has been preparing for
  the Independent Cities Association conference that's happening this week. He
  mentioned he also attended South Bay City's Council of Government's meeting at
  Nakaoka as they recognized Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka for his last meeting. He also
  thanked the IT team for the level of our Wi-Fi and the speed everyone was impressed.
  He continued to say that folks don't get to come over here to Gardena often, but when
  they come over, they're impressed with what we're doing; our big Gardena sign out front
  still blows everybody away. He then thanked the staff and everybody for all his emails
  and phone calls and responding to the issues.

  3) MAYOR PRO TEM TANAKA - Since the last meeting, the City hosted the South Bay
  COG’s monthly meeting at the Nakaoka Center. He mentioned this meeting was his last
  as chairman and he thanked Jackie Bacharach and the entire COG staff for making his
  year a great success and all the support that was given. He then congratulated the Chief
  on his official promotion and badge pinning; it was a great event. He hoped everybody
  had a great 4th. He wasn’t able to attend Rowley Park's 4th of July event, but he did see
  it from his vantage point. He thanked Gardena because there were way fewer illegal
  fireworks than last year and the year before, and said he appreciates that we tried to
  keep it safe and sane this year.

  4) MAYOR CERDA - She attended a couple of events. The first one was the Lions Club, as
  their president had his final sendoff, Steve Makshanoff, and she was there to
  congratulate him; she attended the Council of Government's meeting with Mayor Pro
  Tem Tanaka, she congratulated him on a job well done; she also attended the 11th
  annual Angel City's gaming opening ceremonies and mentioned it’s an organization that
  helps young disabled people play all sorts of games, it was a pre-special Olympics, and
  this was held at El Camino College. She also had her monthly town hall meeting. Her
  topic this time was making sure that people know their constitutional rights as human
  beings, with all that's going on. She also attended the Gardena Valley JCI Matsuri
  Festival. She also attended the Rowley Park 4th of July celebration. She thanked the
  staff as always for doing an amazing job out there. She attended the third annual City of
  Inglewood's music festival that was hosted by Council Member Dionne Faulk and it was
  a great event that was co-sponsored by KJLH. She attended the funeral services for Mr.
  Duane Hinds, who was a former planning commissioner for about 10 years, back in the
  early 90s. Then lastly, she was at our new Chief of Police’s pinning ceremony. She
  congratulated him.

  8
 Docusign Envelope ID: 8B6CAA2E-B1CE-4716-9829-35A467FCDFDC

  5) COUNCIL MEMBER LOVE – She started by sending her condolences to Pastor Ware,
  his wife, and their family for the loss of his father. She apologized to our new Chief of
  Police, Fox, for not attending the ceremony. She mentioned that she had a new
  employee that started and everything that could go wrong went wrong. To the young
  man who spoke during Oral communication, she received an invitation to that protest.
  Unfortunately, she received it at the last minute, and it was a conflict in her schedule,
  and she could not attend. But she wholeheartedly supports you guys, and she does stand
  with you guys. There’s not a lot that our officers can do except stand against it but
  understand they can't get involved. You mentioned ICE being on Gardena Boulevard in
  our surrounding cities. She had a friend show her a video of ICE picking up people right
  here at the corner market. So, ICE is in Gardena. She just wants you to know that. She
  thanked everybody who came out and supported the Gardena Chamber of Fireworks
